map.按入炉金属料、合格连铸坯（锭）与合格成品材的重量，分两级统计金属收得率与成材率，: From the weights of metallic charge fed, qualified cast billet (ingot) and qualified finished product, compute metal yield and product rate at two levels, plus the combined product rate and metal loss, to measure metal loss across the process and processing efficiency. Data is processed only locally in the browser and never uploaded.
map.收得率 = 合格坯（锭）量 ÷ 入炉金属料 × 100%: Yield rate = qualified billet (ingot) ÷ metallic charge × 100%
map.成材率 = 合格成品材量 ÷ 合格坯（锭）量 × 100%: Product rate = qualified finished product ÷ qualified billet (ingot) × 100%

map.📚 深度解析：金属收得率与成材率统计: 📚 In-Depth Analysis: Metal Yield and Product Rate Statistics
map.炼钢/轧制统计金属收得率与成材率，衡量工序金属流失与加工效率。: Compute metal yield and product rate for steelmaking and rolling to measure metal loss across the process and processing efficiency.
map.按单炉次或单批次录入，横向对比不同班组、不同钢种的收得率与成材率差异。: Enter by heat or by batch to compare yield and product rate differences across crews and steel grades.

map.金属收得率 = 产出金属量 ÷ 投入金属量 × 100%；成材率 = 合格产品量: Metal yield = metal output ÷ metal input × 100%; product rate = qualified product ÷ raw material × 100%.
map.投 100 t 原料出合格材 92 t，则成材率 = 92%。10 炉收得率(%: Feeding 100 t of raw material yields 92 t of qualified product, so the product rate = 92%. Yield rates (%) for 10 heats: 91, 93, 92, 90, 94, 92, 93, 91, 92, 95; mean 92.3%, range 95 − 90 = 5%, standard deviation about 1.4%. A heat dropping to 85% is a clear deviation and oxidation or metal-loss issues should be investigated.
map.收得率和成材率差在哪？: How do yield rate and product rate differ?
map.收得率看冶炼环节金属回收（产出/投入），成材率看加工环节合格品比例（合格品/原料: Yield rate looks at metal recovery in the smelting step (output / input), while product rate looks at the qualified proportion in the processing step (qualified product / raw material). The former includes melt loss, the latter includes processing scrap.
map.极差大说明什么？: What does a large range mean?
map.极差与标准差大表示炉次间波动大，工艺或原料不稳定；连续监控可提前发现设备劣化或操: A large range or standard deviation means large variation between heats, so the process or raw material is unstable. Continuous monitoring reveals equipment degradation or operational drift early.
